title: Windowed-access KV workload harness: p95 / hit-rate / memory tradeoff + regression detector
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Goal: build a reproducible synthetic harness that measures tokens/sec throughput and tail latency (p95/p99) against a matrix of KV prefix cache hit rates and memory budgets. The harness must support: (1) windowed access patterns that simulate short-term hotkey bursts, (2) parametric generation of skew (zipf alpha / multi-modal hotset), (3) direct measurement of tokens/sec and token-level p95, and (4) a regression-detection pipeline that flags statistically significant degradations vs baseline runs. Success criteria: able to detect a 10% p95 regression with >90% power on our standard hotkey scenario at 95th percentile traffic burst, and produce a reproducible report + CI gate integration.
experimental_plan: 1) Trace synthesis: transform anonymized production prefix-access traces into a windowed access generator (parameters: window_size=1s/10s, hotspot_fraction=1%, zipf_alpha=1.1..2.0). 2) Baseline matrix: run baseline across memory budgets [2GB, 4GB, 8GB] and hit-rate targets [70%, 80%, 90%]. 3) Metrics: tokens/sec, p95 token latency end-to-end, kv-lookup p95, allocation memory, eviction rate, miss amplification. 4) Statistical tests: use bootstrap CIs for p95, Mann-Whitney U for non-parametric shift detection, and an EWMA-based anomaly score for time-series drift detection. 5) Regression detection: compare candidate run to baseline using two-sided tests and pairwise bootstrapped p95 deltas; produce a single regression score and a human-readable verdict. 6) CI integration: when regression score exceeds threshold, fail pipeline and attach PDF report.
implementation_notes: - Harness implemented in Go with the existing 'load-runner' infra; new module kvwindow_gen. - Uses the runtime's metrics endpoint for per-token latencies (wraps token emission to attribute latencies). - To reduce noise we run each cell of the matrix 6 times and aggregate via median-of-means for tokens/sec and bootstrap for p95. - Persist raw traces and summaries to s3://redwood-perf/kvwindow/ENG-124568/ for later analysis. - Performance counter hooks added to runtime-1.22 branch (PR linked below).
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Initial sketch completed. Chose bootstrap+Mann-Whitney for p95/regression because p95 distributions are heavy-tailed and asymmetrical.
2025-02-12: Implemented trace transformer and windowed generator; validated synthetic trace shape matches production heatmaps (Jensen-Shannon divergence < 0.08 for access distribution).
2025-02-14: Core harness runs stable in local cluster; discovered that short windows (<2s) increase p95 variance — added adaptive replication to stabilize estimates.

2025-02-16: Ran first baseline matrix (2GB/4GB/8GB x 70/80/90 hit) on dedicated staging cluster. Observed an unexpected 12% p95 increase at 80% hit for 4GB budget compared to baseline: triaged to prefetch change on runtime-1.22 branch.
2025-02-17: Re-ran with prefetch disabled -> p95 drop back to baseline. Created PR to gate prefetch heuristics under a runtime flag; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
2025-02-18: Added regression-detector pipeline that emits a JSON verdict and a human-readable PDF summary. Hooked detector into Jenkins perf job for nightly runs.
review_feedback: 2025-02-15 | Daniel Park (reviewer): Recommend adding Mann-Whitney U test plus a simple effect-size (Hodges-Lehmann) for p95 deltas; otherwise OK.
2025-02-16 | Asha Mehta (SRE): Need to run with more realistic burstiness (we should add power-law burst intervals). Also request to tag cluster snapshot IDs in artifacts.
2025-02-17 | Maya Liu (assignee): Implemented effect-size estimate and added cluster-snapshot tagging to upload metadata.
open_tasks: Stabilize CI flakiness: some nightly runs have spurious p95 spikes during network jitter periods -> investigate sampling/isolated infra noise.
Add synthetic 'mixed-traffic' scenario that blends short window bursts with long-tail background traffic (to better reflect prod).
Parameterize detector thresholds by baseline variance per cell (automatic thresholding) and surface in console as recommended SLOs.
Coordinate with PerfEng to add this harness to pre-merge gate for runtime-1.22 PRs that touch prefetch / eviction heuristics.
resolution_criteria: 1) Regression detector integrated into nightly CI and fails reliably on injected regressions (we will run 10 synthetic injection experiments to validate power). 2) Documented runbook for interpreting the report and following up (links in Confluence). 3) Perf-Engineering signoff and a follow-up task to add alerting to Console for customer-facing regressions.
